name: Kaynes Technology India Ltd
about: Incorporated in 2008, Kaynes Technology is a leading end-to-end and IoT solutions-enabled integrated electronics manufacturing company. The company provides conceptual design, process engineering, integrated manufacturing, and life-cycle support for major players in the automotive, industrial, aerospace and defense, outer-space, nuclear, medical, railways, Internet of Things ("IoT"), Information Technology ("IT") and other segments. [1]

statements.text: Revenue compounded 53.9% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 105.2%.
EBITDA margin expanded 590 bps over 5 years (10.0% → 15.9%).
Revenue growth slowed from 58% to 41% YoY over the last 4 quarters.
Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 15.6%, 120 bps below a year ago.
Over 5 years: ₹977 cr of profit, −₹615 cr of operating cash — conversion -0.63x — profits are not turning into cash.

flags.text: Profits not turning into cash: 5-yr CFO/PAT -0.63x
Large capex underway: CWIP ₹511 cr = 32% of fixed assets

ledger.quote: by end of the financial year we'll turn the cash positive
ledger.statement: Cash-positive (operating cash flow) by end of FY27
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: FY27 has not ended. The starting point is weak: Q1 FY27 working capital absorbed about INR259 crore, with inventory up INR177 crore and receivables up INR68 crore (C3). The same promise for FY26 (G15) was not met and has been rolled into this one. 5-year CFO/PAT is -0.63 (F:cfo_to_pat_5y).

ledger.quote: we are pretty confident that we will be able to do the turnaround by end of this year in terms of receivables from the metering business
ledger.statement: Metering-business receivables turnaround by end of FY27
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: FY27 has not ended. In Q1 FY27 receivables still rose INR68-90 crore, mainly in metering (C3), and floods slowed installations (C1). Management responded by cutting metering sales to force collections (C1). The earlier receivable promises (G23, G24) have no confirmed delivery.

ledger.quote: is about INR300 crores for OSAT, INR300 crores for PCB, and about INR250 crores for EMS business
ledger.statement: FY27 capex of about INR 850 crore: OSAT 300, PCB 300, EMS 250
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: Q1 FY27 capex was about INR230 crore (OSAT 90, PCB 90, EMS 50), 27% of the INR850 crore plan with a quarter of the year gone, and management said it is on track (C5). C5 also says modular expansion will continue as new business arrives, so INR850 crore is not a ceiling.

ledger.quote: we have committed a full year revenue of totally INR500 crores between both
ledger.statement: OSAT and PCB full-year FY27 revenue of INR 450-500 crore, starting Q3
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: Revenue is due to start in Q3 FY27 and none is reported yet. INR450-500 crore is below the INR550-700 crore implied by the Q4 FY26 production-value ranges for PCB (G12) and OSAT (G13), so the bar may already have been lowered.

ledger.quote: we have committed the 2x of the market growth
ledger.statement: Revenue growth of 2x the market growth (no absolute number given)
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: Using management's own 16-18% market growth (G7), the bar is 32-36%. Q1 FY27 revenue grew 40.6% (F:rev_yoy_last_q_pct) and FY26 about 33% (C7), but Q3 and Q4 FY26 grew only 21.6% and 26.3% (F:rev_yoy_last4_pct). Market growth is management-stated, not independently measured.

ledger.quote: our goal is to steadily increase the contribution of NPD-led and value-added solutions to nearly 30% of the total revenue in the coming years
ledger.statement: NPD-led and value-added solutions to reach nearly 30% of revenue
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: No NPD or value-added revenue mix is disclosed, and no date was given beyond 'the coming years'.

ledger.quote: we'll double the growth of market growth is what the commitment that we have done
ledger.statement: Revenue growth at twice the EMS market growth (market 16-18%)
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: Same commitment as G5. With the stated 16-18% market growth the bar is 32-36%. Q1 FY27 growth was 40.6% (F:rev_yoy_last_q_pct) and FY26 about 33% (C7), but Q3 and Q4 FY26 at 21.6% and 26.3% fell short (F:rev_yoy_last4_pct).
ledger.actual_text: 40.6% YoY in Q1 FY27; ~33% in FY26

ledger.quote: So rail business, I'm expecting this year to grow by around 20%, 25%
ledger.statement: Rail business growth of 20-25% in FY27
ledger.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan
ledger.evidence: Rail revenue is not disclosed. C2 says railways grew in Q1 FY27 but gives no number.

ledger.quote: the margins are going to be north of current 30% plus
ledger.statement: Rail margins above 30% in FY27
ledger.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan
ledger.evidence: Rail margins are not disclosed in the inputs. C2 says railways grew in Q1 FY27 but gives no margin, so this may end up unverifiable.

ledger.quote: That is why I have committed that it will take up to the third quarter for us to complete this.
ledger.statement: Complete smart-meter installations by Q3FY27
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: Q3 FY27 is under way with no later update. The Q1 FY27 call said floods disrupted installation sites and metering was deliberately scaled back pending collections (C1). Q1 metering revenue fell to INR210 crore (C2).

ledger.quote: For the next year, while the INR971 crores of sales, what we did this year, in absolute numbers, we may remain same or slightly up or down
ledger.statement: Smart-meter sales of about INR971 crore in FY27, roughly flat
ledger.speaker: N. Muthukumar
ledger.evidence: Q1 FY27 metering revenue of INR210 crore (C2) annualises to INR840 crore, 13.5% below the INR971 crore FY26 level. Management says it chose to shrink metering until collections improve (C1).

ledger.quote: PCB of around INR300 crores to INR400 crores
ledger.statement: PCB production value of INR300-400 crore
ledger.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan
ledger.evidence: No horizon was given and no PCB output is reported yet. If it was meant for FY27, the Q1 FY27 commitment of INR450-500 crore for OSAT and PCB combined (G4) sits below the INR550-700 crore implied by this range plus G13.

ledger.quote: OSAT of around INR250 crores to INR300 crores
ledger.statement: OSAT production value of INR250-300 crore
ledger.speaker: Ramesh Kunhikannan
ledger.evidence: No horizon was given and no OSAT output is reported yet. With G12 it implies INR550-700 crore, against the later INR450-500 crore combined FY27 revenue commitment (G4).

ledger.quote: we'll cross about INR4,000 crores minimum
ledger.statement: FY26 revenue of at least INR 4,000 crore including Q4
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: Check: FY26 revenue INR3,626 crore against at least INR4,000 crore, 9.4% short. The INR4,000 crore floor was itself a cut from the original INR4,500 crore guide (C6), so the outcome was 19.4% below the starting guide. Management blamed a ~90% revenue drop at its largest EV customer and two delayed government orders (C7, C8).

ledger.quote: at consol level, we'll definitely be OCF positive by end of this year
ledger.statement: Consolidated operating cash flow positive by end of FY26
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: FY26 has ended. FY26 operating cash flow is not in the inputs, but the Q1 FY27 call re-issued the same promise with a deadline a year later (G1). The Q4 FY26 call said total working capital rose because of metering (C9), and 5-year CFO/PAT is -0.63 (F:cfo_to_pat_5y). Marked missed on that inference.
ledger.actual_text: Not reported; target rolled to FY27

ledger.quote: At a consol level, we'll definitely deliver this number of $1 billion.
ledger.statement: Consolidated revenue of USD 1 billion in FY28, with individual targets possibly higher
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: FY28 target, too early. The inputs give no INR/USD rate to measure the gap from TTM revenue of INR3,899 crore (F:ttm_revenue_cr), and there is no rupee FY27 revenue guide to bridge it.

ledger.quote: maybe about another INR400-odd crores of capex will be spent
ledger.statement: Further capex of about INR 400 crore in the rest of FY26
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: FY26 capex is not in the inputs, so the ~INR400 crore spend planned for the rest of FY26 can't be checked. 5-year FCF is -INR3,287 crore (F:fcf_5y_cr).

ledger.quote: we'll spend about cumulatively INR1,400 crores in the PC Board business
ledger.statement: Cumulative PC Board capex of INR 1,400 crore in FY27 (Phase 1 completed)
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: The FY27 PCB budget is INR300 crore (G3) and about INR90 crore was spent in Q1 (C5). Reaching INR1,400 crore cumulative needs ~INR1,100 crore to have been spent before FY27, which the inputs don't show.
ledger.actual_text: ~INR90 crore PCB capex in Q1 FY27

ledger.quote: which will total up to about between INR700 crores and INR800 crores of smart metering business for the year
ledger.statement: Smart metering revenue of INR 700-800 crore in FY26
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: FY26 smart-meter sales were INR971 crore per the Q4 FY26 call (G11), above the INR700-800 crore range. The figure comes from management, not reported segment data. The extra volume came with receivables: on the Q4 FY26 call metering was ~25% of revenue but 67% of receivables (C9).

ledger.quote: we are not going to implement any more capex in the EMS business
ledger.statement: No EMS capex beyond committed numbers; only debottlenecking spend
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: The FY27 plan includes INR250 crore of EMS capex (G3, C5), and the Q1 FY27 call added that modular capacity expansion will go on as new business arrives (C5), which reopens the no-new-EMS-capex line. The inputs don't say whether the INR250 crore is debottlenecking.
ledger.actual_text: INR250 crore EMS capex planned for FY27; ~INR50 crore spent in Q1

ledger.quote: First balance requirement for OSAT INR10.3 billion will be funded through QIP
ledger.statement: OSAT facility capex requirement of INR 10.3 billion, balance funded from internal accruals over five years
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: Five-year plan. FY27 OSAT capex is INR300 crore (G3), with about INR90 crore spent in Q1 (C5). Funding the balance from internal accruals sits poorly with 5-year FCF of -INR3,287 crore (F:fcf_5y_cr).

ledger.quote: the current plan includes only capex of 14 billion
ledger.statement: PCB business capex plan of INR 14 billion (expansion to be evaluated after state subsidy talks)
ledger.speaker: Jairam Sampath
ledger.evidence: Cumulative PCB spend is not disclosed; the FY27 PCB budget is INR300 crore (G3). Expansion beyond INR14 billion depends on state-subsidy talks, with no update in the inputs.

ledger.quote: approximately INR240 crores of such receivables will anyway get discounted
ledger.statement: About INR 240 crore of smart-meter receivables to be discounted, reducing the receivable balance
ledger.speaker: Management
ledger.evidence: No later call says whether the ~INR240 crore was discounted. Q1 FY27 receivables still rose, mainly in metering (C3), and CCC is 193 days against 162 three years ago (F:ccc_days_latest, F:ccc_days_3y_ago).

ledger.quote: we will endeavor to make sure that these do not cross collection periods of 90 days
ledger.statement: Keep smart-meter receivables within 90-day collection periods (endeavour, not firm)
ledger.speaker: Management
ledger.evidence: Metering collection days are not disclosed. On the Q4 FY26 call, though, metering was ~25% of revenue and 67% of receivables while EMS was 65% of revenue and 35% of receivables (C9), so metering ties up about five times as much in receivables per rupee of sales. Q1 FY27 receivables rose again, mainly in metering (C3). Management now targets a metering receivables turnaround only by end FY27 (G2).

ledger.quote: will help us to do good revenues, starting from FY '27 onwards
ledger.statement: Approvals from three customers expected to support revenue from FY27 onwards
ledger.speaker: Then there is railway -

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management says it is on target for capex, OSAT and PCB revenue and a cash-positive year-end, and says it has improved on last quarter's commitments, though it declines to give an absolute revenue number.

tones.label: defensive
tones.why: Management acknowledges the missed guidance and apologises ("it is not a denied order, it is a delayed order") while reasserting its targets.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management commits to revenue above INR 4,000 crore, consolidated OCF positivity and USD 1 billion revenue in FY28, while declining to give quarterly guidance because a railway product was postponed.

tones.label: defensive
tones.why: Management rebuts analyst-report claims point by point, saying the cited 28% margin appears incorrect and that the observations are not based on facts (p3-18-2).

context.speaker: N. Muthukumar
context.text: Thank you, Mr. Ramesh, and very good morning to everyone. Thank you all for taking the time to join us today. Mr. Ramesh explained about our revenue growth and EBITDA, how we have performed, and also what are the strategic initiatives. Achieving a 40% year-on-year growth in the Q1 and looking at the numbers, this has been specifically come with a reduction in the growth of about smart metering business when compared to Q1. We have taken the feedback of various stakeholders, and looking at the current situation of our balance sheet constraint, we have taken a conscious decision of growing more in EMS business, which is our traditional and core business, and we have degrown in the smart metering business, not because we don't have capacity, not because we don't have business and orders, but we put our foot down saying that we need to make a collection first to make sure that we continue to supply. The current situation in the places where we are doing the installation of meter, due to the natural calamity of flood, which has also impacted this, but keeping everything, our objective of bringing the balance sheet to a better shape, we degrew. But our team, of the leadership team, the operating team did an excellent job of growing in the EMS business. Standalone our EMS business grown much, much higher than the 40% overall growth. There was a promising top-line growth, we agree, but as Mr. Ramesh said, we at Kaynes and our Board of Directors don't look at for a quarter-to-quarter, but for a long-term strategy. But when the growth is good, we also see the impacts on margins due to cost escalation driven by global supply chain issues and the macro factors, such as rise in the energy and the crude prices, the commodity prices, and the forex movement, which in turn led to a rise

That is the split between the EMS. That's why we said our EMS business core growth has gone more than that. In fact, segment-wise, even though we don't specifically, the aerospace business and all is one which we have grown substantially up. Every segment, be it railways, be it automotive, be it aerospace, defense, every segment after segment we have grown. For your exact point on the growth percentages, in a stand-alone EMS business, which it includes other than metering business if you take it, and of course, other than foreign entities also, because our acquisition of the August Electronics was done only in July, so last year first quarter it was not there. So as a stand-alone EMS business if you see, our growth is 53%, fr

context.speaker: N. Muthukumar
context.text: At the end of first quarter, I think we -- as we said, our inventory has gone up by INR177 crores, we have added up, and receivables we were short by INR68 crores, taking it to about a total of about INR259 crores of a negative cash flow, okay? Having said that, the first quarter is very, very challenging quarter in terms of our businesses for most of the Indian entities. I just wanted to bring it to your comparison that Q1 of last year, our negative cash flow was to the level of INR379 crores. Page 10 of 19 Kaynes Technology India Limited August 08, 2026 The team did a remarkable challenges in doing this. Except for the inventory, I think the receivables, the negative was only INR90 crores, mainly because of metering. And in terms of EMS business, the team has done an extremely good job. Inventory is a strategic division. So we have improved on our commitments whatever we have told, and we will ensure that going forward, our commitments of last quarter to deliver the [inaudible 0:34:13] will happen.

Though our inventory levels in terms of the working capital has gone up by about INR150 crores, as I said, this is a strategic decision that we took in the month of February, looking at the global market situation and the volatility. Just because our team has added upon the inventory there, we could able to successfully grow at 40% of plus as an overall, and EMS business alone about 48%. This has -- this inventory increase has helped us, and this will also take us to the next level. We also talked to you earlier about some delayed delivery for a government product.

Sir, we have communicated and we are standing by that. We said we will be funding for this capex for this year is about INR300 crores for OSAT, INR300 crores for PCB, and about INR250 crores for EMS business. We are on track for that. The first quarter spent is about INR90 plus INR90, INR180 plus INR50, INR230 crores, all put together. But we also said that, fund is not a problem, and as and when we get the newer business, the modular capacity expansions will go on. So, and also as and when the subsidies coming, it will keep flowing into the system. This is just to keep a tight control on the cash flows.

Thank you very much for asking this question. We fully understand and appreciate your question. We did an aggressive top line growth in the year based on the order book and we got the electrification of the vehicle. And of course, the government projects where we are working is going to be at the faster pace. Giving a guidance of INR4,500 crores is almost 55% growth over the previous year. In the third quarter, I think we have turned out to saying about INR4,000 crores because of a few delays.

And one of the largest electric vehicle OEM manufacturers has completely dropped by about 90% of the revenue, wherein we were the single supplier which has dropped our numbers. But we were quite confident in the last quarter of getting 2 government orders where the products have been done and the product testing have been approved. It is going to be done, but there is a delayed project. I think these are the 2 things that while we have delivered about 33% growth in revenue and 39% growth in the bottom line, we sincerely understand and appreciate that the guidance what we have given, we could not meet.

Yes. See, what happened is, while we have got the indication from the invoice from the customer, we started ordering the material. And in fact, if you ask us, we have started even the pre-manufacturing activities of this, which gave us the confidence that, yes, we'll be able to deliver. If you see, more than 50% of the manufacturing of those activities also has been in the pipeline. As I said, it is not a denied order, it is a delayed order. We sincerely apologize for that this has happened. But I'm sure that you would all trust me that it is beyond our control.

With various activities of the various state governments releasing the tender for supplying the meter, installing the meter, going to those houses and installing, there was a little delay. I would request you all to appreciate that as a stand-alone Kaynes EMS business, our net working capital days has come from 64 days to 54 days. However, the total number has gone up because of this. 65% of our revenue comes from EMS business where our receivables is only 35%, whereas 25% of the business comes from EMS where the receivables is 67%. We have worked out the strategy with the management team on how to mitigate this.

business.what_it_does: Electronics manufacturing services (EMS) for railways, automotive (including EVs), aerospace and defence customers. It also runs a smart-metering business (supply and installation under state-government tenders) and is building OSAT and PCB businesses whose revenue is due to start in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: EMS
segments.comment: Q1 FY27: about INR736 crore of INR946 crore (C2), growing ~48% YoY against 40% for the company (C4). The Q4 FY26 call put EMS at ~65% of revenue (C9).

segments.name: Smart metering
segments.comment: Q1 FY27: INR210 crore of INR946 crore (C2), deliberately cut back until collections improve (C1). FY26 sales were INR971 crore, ~27% of INR3,626 crore (G11, G14). It carries most of the receivables (C9).

segments.name: OSAT
segments.comment: No revenue yet. FY27 capex INR300 crore (G3). OSAT plus PCB guided at INR450-500 crore of FY27 revenue starting Q3 (G4).

segments.name: PCB
segments.comment: No revenue yet. FY27 capex INR300 crore (G3) within a cumulative plan of INR1,400 crore (G18, G22).

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Q1 FY27 growth of 40%, with EMS up ~48% and metering deliberately shrunk, shows a healthy core business (C1, C4).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Revenue did rise 40.6% YoY, but PAT fell 25.3% and the margin was 15.6% against 16.8% a year earlier. A 120bps margin dip cannot explain a 66-point gap between revenue and profit growth, so the drag sits below the operating line, and the inputs don't explain it.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Balance-sheet repair is the priority: Q1 cash burn of INR259 crore beat last year's INR379 crore, and management says it has 'improved on our commitments' (C3).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: CCC is 193 days against 162 three years ago, 5-year FCF is -INR3,287 crore and 5-year CFO/PAT is -0.63. The FY26 OCF-positive target (G15) was not met and has moved to FY27 (G1).

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Growth is being shifted from metering back to the core EMS business (C1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Metering was INR210 crore of INR946 crore in Q1 FY27 (22%), against INR971 crore of INR3,626 crore in FY26 (27%). The mix shift shows in the numbers.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: The FY26 shortfall came from government orders that are 'delayed, not denied' (C7, C8).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Growth rebounded to 40.6% in Q1 FY27 from 21.6% and 26.3% in Q3 and Q4 FY26. But the Q1 FY27 call still mentions a delayed government delivery (C4), and no input confirms that the two orders have shipped.

bull.point: Core EMS is carrying growth: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 40.6% YoY to INR946 crore, with EMS at ~INR736 crore and growing ~48% while metering shrank.
Long-run compounding: revenue CAGR is 47.7% over 3 years and 53.9% over 5, PAT CAGR is 56.5% over 3 years, and the margin is up 590bps over 5 years.

The capacity build is funded and on schedule: D/E is 0.19 on INR913 crore of borrowings, INR230 crore of the INR850 crore FY27 capex was spent in Q1, and OSAT plus PCB are due to add INR450-500 crore of revenue from Q3 FY27.

bear.point: Cash conversion is negative: 5-year FCF is -INR3,287 crore, CFO/PAT -0.63, CCC 193 days (162 three years ago), and the OCF-positive date has slipped from FY26 to FY27.
Guidance was cut and still missed: the FY26 revenue guide went from INR4,500 crore to INR4,000 crore, and the actual was INR3,626 crore, 19% below the original.
Returns are thin while the capital base grows: ROCE is 13% and Q1 PAT fell 25.3% on 40.6% revenue growth, while the OSAT (INR10.3 billion) and PCB (INR14 billion) plans add capital ahead of revenue.

questions: What was FY26 consolidated operating cash flow, how much of the ~INR240 crore of metering receivables was actually discounted, and what collection days is metering running at against the 90-day ceiling?
Q1 FY27 PAT fell 25.3% while revenue rose 40.6% and the margin dipped only 120bps. How much of the gap is depreciation, interest and OSAT/PCB start-up cost, and when does it reverse?

The Q4 FY26 call implied INR550-700 crore of PCB plus OSAT production value, but the Q1 FY27 call committed INR450-500 crore of FY27 revenue starting Q3. Is that a cut, and which customer qualifications are complete?
